### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14 and A15 were not observed at all (0 of 200 traces); in the later window, A14 appears in about 44 in 100 traces (88 of 200) and A15 in about 56 in 100 traces (111 of 200), in each case exactly once when present. [OCC001, OCC002]
- In the later window, A14 and A15 behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: about 44 in 100 traces contain only A14, about 56 in 100 contain only A15, about 1 in 200 contain neither, and the two never occur in the same trace. In the earlier window, neither activity appeared. [REL001]
- In the earlier window, the outgoing transitions of A35 went to A20 in essentially every case; in the later window they go to A15 in about 56 in 100 cases and to A14 in about 44 in 100, with a direct A35→A20 transition remaining in only about 1 in 200 cases. [DIR003]
- In the later window, all observed outgoing transitions of A14 and of A15 lead to A20. [DIR001, DIR002]
- In the later window, A35 precedes A14 and A15 in every trace where they co-occur, and A14/A15 precede A20 in every such trace; earlier, A20 always appeared without A14 or A15. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- The step distance from A35 to A20 moved from 1 in essentially all earlier traces to 2 in about 99.5 in 100 later traces, consistent with exactly one activity now sitting between them. [LAG001]
- Both new activities occur at a similar mean relative position of about 0.36 of the trace (medians about 0.35). [POS001, POS002]
- All thirteen evidence items show differences larger than roughly 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, an exclusive choice between A14 and A15 was inserted between A35 and A20: A35 now leads to A15 in about 56 in 100 traces and to A14 in about 44 in 100, and the chosen activity then leads on to A20, whereas earlier A35 led directly to A20 and neither A14 nor A15 was observed. A short direct A35→A20 path remains in about 1 in 200 later traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001]

The hypothesis is supported directly and consistently: participation rises from zero to 44% and 56%, both new activities point exclusively to A20, A35's outgoing flow redistributes to exactly these two activities, the order relations place A35 before and A20 after them, A14 and A15 never co-occur, and the A35→A20 distance grows by exactly one step. The number of qualifying items (13) is many times the roughly 0.33 expected if nothing had changed, so chance alone cannot explain the evidence as a whole. [DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL005, LAG001]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A14 and A15 were not observed then, so the evidence cannot distinguish a newly added step from a branch that existed before but went unobserved in the earlier sample; the driver of the roughly 44/56 split between A14 and A15 is also not observable. In addition, many items describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations of one another. [OCC001, OCC002]

Let me analyze this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 67 units tested, 0.33 items expected without change.
- Evidence items: 13 items (OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, REL001–REL005, LAG001).

Screening comparison: 13 items vs 0.33 expected. 13 is many times larger than 0.33 (about 40x), so chance as a whole cannot explain the count. So we move past "insufficient evidence" based on count.

Now let's understand the behaviour.

OCC001: A14 — before: 0 occurrences, 0% participation; after: 0.44 mean occurrences per trace, 44% participation (88 of 200 traces). Recurrence support 0 (each trace contains A14 at most once). Empirical strength ~0.995.

OCC002: A15 — before: 0; after: 0.555 mean, 55.5% participation (111 of 200 traces). Recurrence support 0.

DIR001: A14 outgoing transitions — before: empty (no observations); after: 100% of outgoing transitions go to A20. Support after: 88.

DIR002: A15 outgoing — before: empty; after: 100% to A20. Support after: 111.

DIR003: A35 outgoing — before: 100% to A20; after: 55.5% to A15, 44% to A14, 0.5% to A20. Support 200/200. So A35 previously always led to A20; now it leads to A15 (about 56 in 100) or A14 (about 44 in 100), almost never directly to A20.

POS001: A14 position — before: no support; after: appears at mean relative position ~0.36 (median ~0.35), support 0.44.

POS002: A15 position — before: no support; after: mean ~0.365, median ~0.346, support 0.555.

REL001: A14 & A15 — before: neither in 100% of traces; after: A14 only in 44%, A15 only in 55.5%, neither in 0.5%, co-occurrence 0. So A14 and A15 never occur together; they are alternatives. In the after window, every trace has exactly one of them (44% A14, 56% A15), and 1 trace has neither.

REL002: A14 & A20 — before: A20 only in 100% (A14 never present); after: co-occurrence 44%, A20 only 56%, A before B (A14 before A20) 44%. So when A14 occurs, it occurs before A20.

REL003: A14 & A35 — before: A35 only 100%; after: co-occurrence 44%, A35 only 56%, B before A (A35 before A14) 44%. So A35 occurs before A14.

REL004: A15 & A20 — before: A20 only 100%; after: co-occurrence 55.5%, A20 only 44.5%, A15 before A20 55.5%. So A15 before A20.

REL005: A15 & A35 — before: A35 only 100%; after: co-occurrence 55.5%, A35 only 44.5%, A35 before A15 55.5%. So A35 before A15.

LAG001: A35 → A20 lag — before: lag 1 in 100%; after: lag 2 in 99.5%. So the distance between A35 and A20 increased from 1 step to 2 steps. This is consistent with a new activity (A14 or A15) being inserted between A35 and A20.

Putting it together:

Before: A35 → A20 directly (lag 1, 100% of traces). A14 and A15 never occur.

After: A35 → A14 (44%) or A15 (56%), then that activity → A20. A14 and A15 are mutually exclusive alternatives (never co-occur). Each occurs exactly once when present (recurrence support 0). A14/A15 appear at relative position ~0.35, i.e., about a third into the trace. A35 before A14/A15; A14/A15 before A20. LAG A35→A20 becomes 2 steps because the new activity sits between them.

So the hypothesis: a new step was inserted between A35 and A20 — an exclusive choice between A14 and A15 (about 44/56 split). This is a structural change: activities A14 and A15 were added (became observed), inserted on the path from A35 to A20 as alternatives.

Wait — but the instructions say "Do not assume that a structural change exists." We need to judge support. The count is 13 vs 0.33 expected — many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it. Then judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competing explanations.

The evidence is highly consistent: OCC (both new activities appear from zero), DIR (both point to A20; A35 now routes to them instead of A20), REL (A35 before A14/A15, A14/A15 before A20, A14 and A15 mutually exclusive), LAG (A35→A20 distance goes from 1 to 2), POS (both at ~0.35 relative position, consistent with being between A35 and A20 if those are at ~1/3 and ~2/3... actually we don't know A35/A20 positions, but the relative position ~0.35 is consistent).

Competing explanations: Could this be a rare variant appearing? A14/A15 appear in 44% and 56% of 200 traces — that's not rare. Zero participation before means not observed in 200 traces; if it were a rare variant that just happened to show up, we'd expect low participation. 44–56% participation in the after window with zero in 200 before traces is a strong change. The empirical strength ~0.995 for all items.

One caveat: "Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window." But with 200 traces before and 44–56% after, the sampling explanation is essentially ruled out by the empirical strength and the screening count.

Another consideration: is this "a shift in how often existing paths are taken"? No — A14 and A15 were (nearly) absent before (zero participation), so it's not a path-frequency shift; it's addition of activities / a new path segment. The hypothesis would be: activities A14 and A15 were added as an exclusive choice between A35 and A20.

Actually, could it be that A14/A15 existed but were never observed? We can't rule that out entirely, but the evidence supports the insertion hypothesis. The instruction says state it as a possibility supported by the evidence, not as a confirmed modification.

Also note: REL001 shows neither A14 nor A15 in 0.5% (1 trace) of after window — so in 1 of 200 after traces, neither occurred; possibly A35→A20 direct still happens rarely (DIR003 shows A35→A20 at 0.005). Consistent.

Also, the LAG001 change: A35→A20 lag goes from 1 to 2 in ~99.5% of traces. This directly shows an activity inserted between them.

So support level: Supported hypothesis.

Main hypothesis: In the later window, a new exclusive choice between A14 and A15 was inserted on the path from A35 to A20: A35 now leads to A15 in about 56 in 100 traces and to A14 in about 44 in 100 (rarely directly to A20), and the chosen activity then leads to A20. Before, A35 led directly to A20 in essentially all traces, and A14/A15 were not observed at all.

Supporting signs:
- Participation: A14 from 0% to 44% (88/200), A15 from 0% to 55.5% (111/200), each occurring once per trace when present (recurrence support 0).
- Direction: A14 and A15 outgoing transitions go to A20 in 100% of observed cases; A35's outgoing transitions changed from 100% A20 to ~56% A15 and ~44% A14, with only ~0.5% direct to A20.
- Relations: A35 before A14 (44%) and before A15 (55.5%); A14 before A20 (44%), A15 before A20 (55.5%); A14 and A15 never co-occur (mutually exclusive alternatives).
- Lag: A35→A20 distance moved from 1 step (100%) to 2 steps (~99.5%), consistent with one activity inserted between them.
- Position: A14 and A15 appear at mean relative position ~0.36, consistent with a single insertion point.
- Consistency: all 13 items align with one underlying difference; count 13 vs 0.33 expected.

Limitations / competing explanations: Zero participation before only shows A14/A15 were not observed in the earlier sample; the evidence cannot show whether they were newly added to the process or previously present but unobserved (e.g., an extremely rare path). Also, the choice mechanism (why 44/56) can't be determined. Also, several items describe the same traces, so they're not independent confirmations — but the screening count comparison handles that (we don't merge items for the count comparison, per instructions: "do not merge items for this comparison").

Wait, re-read: "A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference; do not merge items for this comparison." So 13 >> 0.33, fine.

Now, is "Supported hypothesis" appropriate? The evidence directly shows: new activities appear, they sit between A35 and A20 in order, they're mutually exclusive, the direct edge A35→A20 nearly disappears, lag increases by exactly 1. This is direct relational evidence (REL, DIR, LAG) supporting an insertion/added-choice hypothesis. Yes, Supported hypothesis.

One nuance: the hypothesis is about "an activity moved/swapped" needing relational evidence — here we have relational evidence. The hypothesis is "activities A14 and A15 were added as an exclusive alternative step between A35 and A20." Supported.

Other differences: LAG001 is part of the main hypothesis (insertion explains lag change). DIR003 also part. Everything fits the one hypothesis. The 1 trace with neither A14 nor A15 and the 0.5% direct A35→A20 — minor residual, can mention as a small residual direct path in about 1 in 200 after traces.

Hmm, is there anything not part of the hypothesis? Not really. Maybe mention that in the after window about 1 in 200 traces still goes A35 directly to A20 without A14/A15 (DIR003 0.005, REL001 neither 0.005) — this is a minor residual consistent with the main hypothesis (the old path retained rarely), not a separate difference.

State hypothesis: In the later window, an exclusive choice between A14 and A15 appears on the path between A35 and A20: A35 leads to A15 in about 56 in 100 traces and to A14 in about 44 in 100, and the chosen activity then leads to A20, whereas earlier A35 led directly to A20 and A14/A15 were not observed.
